title: Subprocessor Disaster Recovery Tabletop Exercise Annex (Draft)
body:
Purpose and scope
This Annex sets an operational and contractual baseline for recurring disaster recovery (DR) tabletop exercises that the Subprocessor must execute and evidence for Redwood Inference. It is intended to be attached to the Master Services Agreement or Data Processing Addendum where the Subprocessor performs inference-serving or related telemetry operations.

High-level objective
- Validate Subprocessor ability to detect, escalate, and recover from service-impacting events that affect availability, data integrity or data access for Redwood workloads within contractually agreed RTO/RPO windows.
- Test communications pathways, evidence collection and remediation planning such that Redwood can reasonably rely on the Subprocessor’s operational continuity.

Key terms (placeholders for insertion into primary contract)
- Exercise cadence: Quarterly tabletop exercises (minimum once per contract year; 1 full-scale run annually).
- Notice window: Redwood will provide at least 30 days’ notice for scheduled exercises; one unscheduled (surprise) exercise per 12 months allowed with 72 hours’ notice and limited scope (no customer-impacting simulated failures).
- Outcomes: Formal Exercise Report and After Action Review (AAR) delivered within 10 business days of exercise completion.
- Evidence: Playbooks, runbooks, alerting screenshots, timeline logs, and remediation task lists must be uploaded to an agreed evidence repository.

Exercise types and sample scenarios
1) Availability outage (control plane)
   - Scenario: A configuration rollout triggers cascading reconnections that cause control-plane API errors for >20% of requests.
   - Goals: Validate detection, rollback procedure, fallback routing, and SLA credit triggering.
   - Simulated injects: Rolling deploy with bad config, increased error rates on monitoring dashboards.

2) Data-access incident (isolation + containment)
   - Scenario: Temporary misrouting causes a customer tenant’s queries to be logged in an ephemeral debug store for 45 minutes.
   - Goals: Confirm notification timelines, log redaction verification, retention policy enforcement, and evidence of secure deletion.
   - Simulated injects: Fake log entries, mock discovery by auditor.

3) KV-cache or model-serving regression (performance degradation)
   - Scenario: Serving runtime introduces a regression that triples median latency on specific prompt shapes.
   - Goals: Test rollback to previous model variant, effectiveness of prefix caching, and customer communication workflow for performance incidents.

4) Key management outage (KMS/HSM unavailability)
   - Scenario: KMS region experiences outage and automated failover does not trigger.
   - Goals: Validate alternate key access procedures, cryptographic key usage logs, and proof of no plaintext exposure.

Exercise conduct (roles and responsibilities)
- Redwood exercise sponsor: Assigns business context, defines success criteria, and identifies impacted logical tenants.
- Subprocessor exercise lead: Coordinates playbook execution, records timelines, aggregates artifacts, and certifies accuracy of the report.
- Observer(s): Redwood security or SRE observers participate to validate fidelity; observers may raise injects during exercise.
- Escalation path: Pre-defined phone/email escalation + on-call rotations; exercise to verify first-hour-to-remediation timeline adherence.

Artifacts and deliverables
1) Pre-exercise checklist (Subprocessor confirms):
   - Confirm exercise scope and non-production vs production boundaries.
   - Identify personnel and contact points.
   - Provision evidence upload location.
2) Exercise logbook (minute-level):
   - Who did what and when, alerts triggered, commands executed, rollbacks initiated.
3) Evidence bundle (at minimum):
   - Monitoring graphs (PNG), alert payloads, relevant runbook excerpts, postmortem templates, sanitized logs.
4) Exercise Report (template required):
   - Executive summary, timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation steps tested, gap analysis vs contractual RTO/RPO, recommended corrective actions, planned re-test date.
5) After Action Review (AAR) video or minutes:
   - Stakeholder attendance, decision points, closure items with owners and deadlines.

Acceptance criteria and success metrics
- Objective completion: Each exercise must hit the three primary objectives (detect, contain, recover) for the simulated incident category.
- RTO verification: Demonstrable recovery within contract RTO +/- 20% for tabletop-simulated paths.
- Evidence completeness: All items in the Evidence bundle checklist present and machine-readable where possible (CSV/JSON).
- Improvement commitments: Any action items assigned must include owners and target dates and be tracked in linked ticketing system.

Remediation, non-conformance, and contractual remedies
- Minor non-conformance: Missed evidence items or incomplete runbook steps — Subprocessor proposes remediation plan and deadline; Redwood retains right to require an accelerated follow-up exercise.
- Major non-conformance: Failure to meet RTO/RPO in exercise, evidence of process gaps that would materially impact customer data or service — escalates to remediation plan with third-party audit option and potential SLA credits or right to terminate for cause per MSA.

Privacy and data handling during exercises
- No real customer data: All exercises must use synthetic or redacted data (explicit examples included in runbook).
- Data minimization: Logs collected for the exercise must be tagged and automatically expired per retention clause.

Confidentiality and use of results
- Exercise outputs are Confidential Information. Redwood may share summary-level results with existing customers where required by contractual transparency obligations, but raw evidence bundles remain Redwood-subprocessor bilateral.

Template clauses for integration into primary agreement
1) Exercise cadence clause (insert):
   - "Subprocessor shall conduct DR tabletop exercises as described in the Subprocessor DR Tabletop Exercise Annex (Quarterly cadence, annual full-scale)."
2) Evidence delivery clause (insert):
   - "Subprocessor shall deliver Exercise Report and Evidence Bundle within ten (10) business days of exercise completion."
3) Audit and remediation clause (insert):
   - "If an exercise surfaces material non-conformance, Redwood may require an independent third-party audit at Subprocessor expense if remediation is not completed within agreed timelines."

Operational notes / Implementation guidance (non-binding)
- Keep the first exercise focused and scoped: target a single critical flow (e.g., control plane deploy rollback) and iterate complexity across quarters.
- Build a sanitized evidence export tool in advance to avoid ad-hoc manual exports that leak real data.
- Use a scoring rubric (detection, containment, recovery) to objectively measure progress across vendors.

Open questions / decisions needed from contract team
- Acceptable tolerance for RTO deviations for tabletop exercises (we propose +/-20%).
- Permissible frequency and scope of surprise exercises (we propose 1 surprise / 12 months).
- Definition of "material non-conformance" and mandatory third-party audit thresholds.

Next steps (drafting checklist)
- Legal: Convert template clauses for MSA/DPA insertion and review termination remedies.
- Security: Produce sanitized-data examples for runbooks.
- SRE/Platform: Create evidence export checklist and tagging schema.
- Procurement: Negotiate exercise cadence and audit rights during vendor onboarding.

Notes to reviewers (internal)
- This is intentionally prescriptive on evidence expectations to avoid later debates during audits.
- Treat this Annex as a living document; we expect minor tweaks after 1st vendor pilot.

End of draft annex.
